item.title: Baker Boy Takes Album, Song and Film Clip of the Year at 2026 NIMAs
item.description:
Here's a short and engaging podcast script based on the article:
[Upbeat music plays in the background]
Host: "Welcome to this week's music news! The 2026 National Indigenous Music Awards were held on August 8th at the Darwin Amphitheater, and what a night it was! Baker Boy took home not one, not two, but three top prizes, including Album of the Year for his latest release, DJANDJAY.
[Short clip of Baker Boy's music plays]
Host: "Baker Boy's single 'THICK SKIN', featuring Thelma Plum, Emma Donovan, Kee'ahn, and Jada Weazel, won both Song of the Year and Film Clip of the Year. And, in a surprise move, he performed the track live at the ceremony with Emma Donovan joining him on stage.
[Short clip of Birdz and Fred Leone's music plays]
Host: "Other big winners of the night included cousin duo Birdz and Fred Leone, who took home Artist of the Year, and Drifting Clouds, who won Best New Talent. The Northern Peninsula Area won Community Clip of the Year for 'All The Way From The NPA', and Bulman School & Community earned the Indigenous Language Award for 'LOK LOK MAH BURARR'.
[Short clip of Saltwater Band's music plays]
Host: "The night also saw the induction of blues musician Marlene Cummins and Elcho Island's Saltwater Band into the NIMAs Hall of Fame. MusicNT's Mark Smith summed up the evening perfectly, saying it was a celebration of the 'incredible music and musicians this country produces, showcasing the rich connection of family and culture'.
[Outro music plays]
Host: "That's all for this week's music news. Congratulations to all the winners of the 2026 National Indigenous Music Awards! We'll be back with more music updates soon. Thanks for tuning in!"
[Outro music continues to play until the end]
